name: Laryngomalacia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and endoscopic diagnosis of laryngomalacia

criteria.description: Inspiratory stridor present since birth or early infancy
Flexible fiberoptic laryngoscopy demonstrating supraglottic collapse or prolapse during inspiration
Exclusion of other causes of stridor such as vocal cord paralysis or subglottic stenosis
Presence of feeding difficulties or failure to thrive supportive but not required

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of inspiratory stridor with characteristic findings on flexible laryngoscopy and exclusion of other causes of stridor
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by endoscopic visualization of supraglottic collapse.

searchTerms: upper airway collapse when breathing in

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties including choking or coughing during feeds
Intermittent cyanosis during feeding or agitation
searchTerms: bluish skin when upset or feeding

occasional.symptomName: Struggling or increased work of breathing

rare.symptomName: Severe airway obstruction requiring surgical intervention
Pulmonary hypertension secondary to chronic hypoxia
searchTerms: lung artery hypertension from low oxygen
pulmonary hypertension due to chronic hypoxia

imaging: Flexible fiberoptic laryngoscopy showing supraglottic collapse during inspiration
Possible chest X-ray to exclude other causes or complications such as pneumonia
other: Clinical observation of stridor and feeding difficulties
Pulse oximetry may show intermittent desaturation

distinguishingFeatures: Unilateral or bilateral vocal cord immobility on laryngoscopy
Fixed airway narrowing below the vocal cords on endoscopy or imaging
Collapse of the trachea rather than supraglottic structures
Stridor or wheezing that worsens with expiration

redFlags: Failure to thrive despite supportive care
references: Kumar S, et al. Laryngomalacia: A review of the literature. Int J Pediatr Otorhinolaryngol. 2019.
Thompson DM. Laryngomalacia: Etiology, diagnosis, and management. Curr Opin Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 2007.
National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD). Laryngomalacia.
